# 2 Baruch Chapter 21 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**1** And I went forth and sat in a cave of the earth in the valley of Kidron, and I fasted there seven days.

**2** And after seven days I lifted up my eyes toward heaven, and I opened my mouth and said:

**3** O Lord my God, you who called the beginning into being from before the ages, and before whom the ages stand, and in whose hand is the passing away of the times —

**4** You whose throne stands in the heights beyond reckoning, and whose glory extends beyond all searching out —

**5** Before whom the armies of the angels stand trembling, and who serve with trembling and with fire before your glory —

**6** To whom there is no beginning, and to whom there is no end; who upheld the living by your word, and who summoned the dead by your command —

**7** You who appointed over the living their number, and over the dead their limits; who does not permit the kings to transgress your commandments —

**8** You who remember all things, and who do not forget anything among all created things —

**9** Hear, O Lord, my prayer, and give heed to my supplication.

**10** For we are, all of us, not many compared to you; we are as though we did not exist at all, and like a drop from a bucket.

**11** We pass away like the morning mist, and our strength is as a vapor.

**12** In your goodness are ordered our days, and in the compassion of your right hand are numbered our years.

**13** For the Most High is great, and the Mighty One is powerful; and he has not forgotten even one among the sons of men.

**14** O Lord, you have heard the prayer of those who have fallen asleep, and you are to be feared before the departed.

**15** Was it not written in former times by the mouth of the prophets, saying: Behold, the days are coming when the Most High will visit the world which he made?

**16** And he will make a reckoning with those who have transgressed the commandment; and he will judge the living by means of the dead, and will requite those who have transgressed with the fruits of their transgression.

**17** And he will raise up those who were sleeping in the dust, and will bring forth the living ones who have waited for him, and will bring into the treasury those who were sealed, so that they may sit down.

**18** And then he will destroy those who have corrupted themselves, and he will deliver those who have polluted themselves to the fire.

**19** And when he has subjected everything that is corruptible and has renewed the age and has revived those who were sleeping in hope of him —

**20** Then shall his rest come.

**21** For you alone are able to do this, and I speak before you.

**22** For your furnace is full, and the abundance of your compassion is being withheld from those who live now.

**23** Yet if you had compassion on those who are now alive, and if you hastened your times and shortened the measure of the ages —

**24** You would not have left your treasury empty, and the coming age would not have been so long delayed.

**25** For great is your strength, O Lord, and great is your glory; great is your beauty, and great is your grace, and great is your compassion. Amen, amen.

**26** And after these things I sat there seven more days.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering from the Syriac Codex Ambrosianus. Chapter 21 contains Baruch's great prayer of intercession, structured as an extended address to God rehearsing his divine attributes before petitioning for the hastening of the end.*
